## Problem and behavior

Normal Decision contention could expose an empty final after `open("wx")`, or observe ENOENT after EEXIST and a legitimate release, producing GATE_CORRUPT before Decision OCC. The approved D1–D4 contract from PR #85 is implemented here; malformed/unverifiable final gates still stop and are never unlocked automatically.

Completed same-directory wx/0600 candidates are file-synced/read back and exclusively hard-linked to final. Directory sync and exact creation-inode/bytes verification precede a live nominal lease. Publication ambiguity returns no authority and retains evidence; release revokes before unlink and never retries against another owner. Namespace races use fresh exclusive attempts bounded to eight retries/one monotonic second within Decision's existing five-second budget.

## Scope and safety

- Update only the approved section10.1 normative deltas, shared Gate publisher/lease, exact candidate classification, Decision budget, direct regressions, Linux Node20/24 CI coverage and minimal operational guidance.
- Discovery retains candidate raw observations; candidates are excluded from generic publisher cleanup and transaction ArtifactRef authority. Orphans are not adopted/deleted/reused.
- Existing schemas/ID rules/hash projections, Recovery predicates, immutable terminal evidence, CLI actions and exit table remain unchanged. The old CLI corrupt-final test now expects the approved own candidate retention while asserting every existing artifact's bytes/inode, exact addition count/structure and unchanged exit8/no dispatch.
- No Production Bootstrap/Apply/Recovery, production data/staging changes, force unlock, bypass, weaker filesystem fallback or SCR-002/API/DB work.

## Evidence

Final runtime/test source ledger: `12f1205d3e7719ea6c6750359236ba4161adeff52645b44c567e32f3b250cc0f` (identical before/after each final run).

| Validation | Actual result |

| Same-device Linux gate/crash | 66 pass / 0 fail / 0 skip / 0 cancelled, exit0; fixture device27 = repo device27 |
| Ordinary unfiltered serial npm test | 795 pass / 0 fail / 1 existing skip / 0 cancelled, exit0; complete TAP/JSONL and unchanged source |
| FN-004 named test files (subset of full) | 627 pass / 0 fail / 1 existing skip / 0 cancelled |
| CLI files (subset) | 44 pass, including18 actual SIGKILL boundaries |
| Rankings / Site | each exit0; anomaly_count0 |
| Markdown | 33 files / 522 links / 16 fragments / broken0 |
| Generated diff / git diff --check | PASS |

Full-run command: `npm test -- --test-concurrency=1 --test-reporter=tap --test-reporter-destination=<TAP> --test-reporter=<JSONL reporter> --test-reporter-destination=<JSONL>`. Duration9,546,461.949ms. The single existing local skip checks the actual GitHub Actions checkout; local fixtures run and CI executes that check. No assertion/timeout/new skip relaxation. The filesystem suite includes14 real gate SIGKILL boundaries and a separate-process link race; existing6A–6F I/O/restart suites passed in the full run.

The forced pre-fix Decision race regression fails on isolated base main, while the new implementation reaches one winner and DECISION_HEAD_CONFLICT for the loser. An actual held-gate probe returns GATE_BUSY after ~5002ms without changing owner bytes or dispatching domain work. A read+close double-I/O regression first failed (47/1, exit1); the implementation now preserves the original EACCES/descriptor and secondary close error. Superseded/interrupted full runs are retained and are not treated as PASS.

FA-M01 remains OPEN for independent review/merge/post-merge verification and separate Final Acceptance. This PR does not declare FN-004 accepted. Actual physical power-loss/storage flush guarantees, volume capacity thresholds/monitoring/evidence retention and a quiescent rollout remain operator prerequisites. No orphan GC or gate-only orphan automatic recovery is added. CI's Node20/24 compatibility and original full/build result must be assessed on this exact PR head.

See `docs/plans/FN-004-FA-M01-Gate-Publication.md` for GP01–GP16 and changed source/test links.

+## GP-A: contract and publication
+
+The normative [recovery contract](../design/FN-004-反映処理・復旧.md), [bootstrap/state contract](../design/FN-004-初期化・ID状態.md), [Decision contract](../design/FN-004-判断モデル.md), [CLI contract](../design/楽曲管理のCLI・画面連携.md) and [operator guide](../canonical-cli.md) contain the section 10.1 deltas before the new runtime connection.
+
+- [Gate publication](../../src/fn004-gate-publication.js) completes metadata in its own same-directory wx/0600 candidate, syncs and verifies the creation inode and exact bytes, then links exclusively to the final name. It syncs the directory, verifies final identity/bytes, removes only its verified candidate, and syncs again. No rename fallback exists.
+- [Gate leases](../../src/fn004-gate.js) retain the original creation descriptor in their private WeakMap. Only after publication, post-acquisition guards and fresh ownership verification does the caller receive a lease. Copied tokens do not confer authority.
+- EEXIST observations use a separate read descriptor and independently validate full v1 metadata/root and the final pathname identity. Stable valid other owners are BUSY. ENOENT is only evidence of a namespace race; it permits a new exclusive attempt, not a fabricated owner/release proof. Invalid bytes already observed cannot be erased by a later disappearance.
+- A link exception leaves publication unknown unless the original inode and bytes are positively observed at final. Even positively observed publication after an exception returns no lease. Failure retains evidence and the original cause/errno/path/phase/descriptor. BUSY cleanup failure also retains the original contention error.
+- Release revokes the lease before close/unlink/sync. Failure reobserves same/absent/other/unknown, preserves the original error and never retries unlink against a later owner. Recovery adoption and retirement ordering remain unchanged.
+
+GateMetadataV1, GateWitness, persisted ErrorEvidence, ID rules, artifact schemas, readiness/action vocabulary and hash projections are unchanged.
+
+## GP-B: all consumers
+
+[Candidate classification](../../src/fn004-gate-candidate.js) recognizes only the exact root-relative lowercase UUIDv4 namespace. [Namespace validation](../../src/fn004-evidence-namespace.js) classifies it before generic publisherTarget. It is not added to the transaction ArtifactRef allowlist. Symlinks/nonregular entries are unsafe. A candidate name disappearing between listing and lstat confers no domain evidence; other listing/inspection errors stop with their typed cause.
+
+This central publisher exclusion covers the existing terminal-runtime, local-evidence, collections, recovery-snapshot and executor cleanup callers. [Raw Discovery](../../src/fn004-evidence-discovery.js) retains candidate path/kind/bytes/hash and does not parse candidates as JSON evidence. Observation v2 remains unchanged; candidate addition/change/removal changes its hash and can reject a stale run. Recovery cleanup neither deletes nor adopts orphan candidates.
+
+[Runtime readiness](../../src/fn004-runtime-state.js) separates exact regular candidates from bootstrap intent/temp and cleanup classification on uninitialized/genesis paths. All bootstrap/state/History/Request/terminal validations remain required. Normal Apply and retry use the existing services, not a new execution path.
+
+[Decision acquisition](../../src/fn004-decision-application.js) shares its existing five-second acquisition budget with [the internal monotonic context](../../src/fn004-gate-budget.js). Namespace relinks remain bounded to eight retries and one second from first contention, limited by the remaining Decision budget. The budget does not cancel an in-flight syscall or callback. Callback entry prevents automatic redispatch. OCC still determines DECISION_HEAD_CONFLICT after acquisition; corrupt gates are not reclassified as ordinary conflicts.
+
+No orphan GC, stale-PID unlock, candidate reuse, forced Recovery, new CLI option, or production operation is introduced. Deploy all participating readers/writers together; mixed old/new writers do not satisfy this contract.

+The normative [recovery contract](../design/FN-004-反映処理・復旧.md), [bootstrap/state contract](../design/FN-004-初期化・ID状態.md), [Decision contract](../design/FN-004-判断モデル.md), [CLI contract](../design/楽曲管理のCLI・画面連携.md) and [operator guide](../canonical-cli.md) contain the section 10.1 deltas before the new runtime connection.
+
+- [Gate publication](../../src/fn004-gate-publication.js) completes metadata in its own same-directory wx/0600 candidate, syncs and verifies the creation inode and exact bytes, then links exclusively to the final name. It syncs the directory, verifies final identity/bytes, removes only its verified candidate, and syncs again. No rename fallback exists.
+- [Gate leases](../../src/fn004-gate.js) retain the original creation descriptor in their private WeakMap. Only after publication, post-acquisition guards and fresh ownership verification does the caller receive a lease. Copied tokens do not confer authority.
+- EEXIST observations use a separate read descriptor and independently validate full v1 metadata/root and the final pathname identity. Stable valid other owners are BUSY. ENOENT is only evidence of a namespace race; it permits a new exclusive attempt, not a fabricated owner/release proof. Invalid bytes already observed cannot be erased by a later disappearance.
+- A link exception leaves publication unknown unless the original inode and bytes are positively observed at final. Even positively observed publication after an exception returns no lease. Failure retains evidence and the original cause/errno/path/phase/descriptor. BUSY cleanup failure also retains the original contention error.
+- Release revokes the lease before close/unlink/sync. Failure reobserves same/absent/other/unknown, preserves the original error and never retries unlink against a later owner. Recovery adoption and retirement ordering remain unchanged.
+
+GateMetadataV1, GateWitness, persisted ErrorEvidence, ID rules, artifact schemas, readiness/action vocabulary and hash projections are unchanged.
+
+## GP-B: all consumers
+
+[Candidate classification](../../src/fn004-gate-candidate.js) recognizes only the exact root-relative lowercase UUIDv4 namespace. [Namespace validation](../../src/fn004-evidence-namespace.js) classifies it before generic publisherTarget. It is not added to the transaction ArtifactRef allowlist. Symlinks/nonregular entries are unsafe. A candidate name disappearing between listing and lstat confers no domain evidence; other listing/inspection errors stop with their typed cause.
+
+This central publisher exclusion covers the existing terminal-runtime, local-evidence, collections, recovery-snapshot and executor cleanup callers. [Raw Discovery](../../src/fn004-evidence-discovery.js) retains candidate path/kind/bytes/hash and does not parse candidates as JSON evidence. Observation v2 remains unchanged; candidate addition/change/removal changes its hash and can reject a stale run. Recovery cleanup neither deletes nor adopts orphan candidates.
+
+[Runtime readiness](../../src/fn004-runtime-state.js) separates exact regular candidates from bootstrap intent/temp and cleanup classification on uninitialized/genesis paths. All bootstrap/state/History/Request/terminal validations remain required. Normal Apply and retry use the existing services, not a new execution path.
+
+[Decision acquisition](../../src/fn004-decision-application.js) shares its existing five-second acquisition budget with [the internal monotonic context](../../src/fn004-gate-budget.js). Namespace relinks remain bounded to eight retries and one second from first contention, limited by the remaining Decision budget. The budget does not cancel an in-flight syscall or callback. Callback entry prevents automatic redispatch. OCC still determines DECISION_HEAD_CONFLICT after acquisition; corrupt gates are not reclassified as ordinary conflicts.
+
+No orphan GC, stale-PID unlock, candidate reuse, forced Recovery, new CLI option, or production operation is introduced. Deploy all participating readers/writers together; mixed old/new writers do not satisfy this contract.
